title: Recovery 2.10 - the LaunchPad wired like the cooker: no USB, bench supply on J22
source: Own photos, raptox's LaunchPad, stitched from photos 04-08 of 2026-11-05 (jumpers as delivered in the photo)
caption: USB out. 3.3 V from the bench supply on J22 (never 5 V there), the CH340's ground on J22's other GND pin, J9 on, J13 on SOP2 only. The jumper column and the CH340's two signal wires: see the drawing rec2-10_launchpad-jumper-column.

callouts.label: unplugged
callouts.note: The XDS110's USB. Out for the whole step: the cooker has no debug probe, so the LaunchPad runs without its USB half (TI SWRU463C 2.6.2 step 1).

callouts.label: 3V3 pin: bench supply +, 3.30 V, limit 100 mA
callouts.note: Printed '3V3' and '+'. TI's 3.3 V (battery) input: a reverse-polarity diode (about 150 mV drop), then the CC3220's supply. No regulator: never 5 V here. On the cooker the bench supply goes to JP5 at 5.0 V instead, into the regulator U17.

callouts.label: GND pin (outer): bench supply −
callouts.note: Printed 'GND' and '−', the pin farthest from 3V3.

callouts.label: GND pin (middle): CH340 GND
callouts.note: Printed 'GND'. One ground for the supply and the adapter.

callouts.label: RST PU: jumper ON
callouts.note: Printed 'J9' and 'RST PU'. The pull-up on the CC3220's nRESET, which TI requires when the board runs from J22 (SWRU463C 2.5.5, 2.6.2 step 3).

callouts.label: one jumper on SOP2 only (as now)
callouts.note: The boot-loader strap, the cooker's X6 pad. SOP1 and SOP0 open; never SOP1 and SOP0 together (factory restore, a write). Close-up: rec2-4_launchpad-j13-sop2.

callouts.label: the jumper column: see the drawing
callouts.note: GND, 5V, VBAT, BRD, RX, TX, RST, TMS, TCK, TDI, TDO, BRD-SENSE. Which caps come off, which one goes across, and the two CH340 wires: rec2-10_launchpad-jumper-column.

callouts.label: FRST: never pressed
callouts.note: Printed 'SW4' and 'FRST': factory restore at reset, which rewrites the flash (SWRU463C table 8).

callouts.label: 5 V input: not used
callouts.note: Printed 'GND GND 5V'. TI's 5 V input; whether it also powers the XDS110 half isn't known without the schematic, so it stays empty.
